retrieved_evidence.excerpt:
[Space Health Research | Spaceflight Cardiovascular Physiology > Cephalad Fluid Redistribution and Cardiovascular Deconditioning in Microgravity]
Title: Cephalad Fluid Redistribution and Cardiovascular Deconditioning in Microgravity
Domain: Spaceflight Cardiovascular Physiology
Citation: NASA-HRP-CARDIO-2024-08

Within hours of orbital insertion, microgravity causes a cephalad redistribution of approximately 1.5 to 2.0 liters of venous blood and interstitial fluid. This central hypervolemia stimulates baroreceptors and atrial natriuretic peptide secretion, causing early plasma volume contraction. Resting heart rate may increase by 5-12 bpm during initial adaptation, and transient subjective head fullness and nasal congestion are standard adaptation symptoms.

[Mission Medical Protocols | Operational Behavioral Medicine > Operational Guidelines for In-Flight Acute Stress and Fatigue Interventions]
Title: Operational Guidelines for In-Flight Acute Stress and Fatigue Interventions
Domain: Operational Behavioral Medicine
Citation: NASA-BHO-STRESS-2024-V2.0

When sensor telemetry detects confirmed acute stress activation (elevated HR, suppressed RMSSD, elevated phasic EDA) accompanied by self-reported cognitive fatigue or anxiety, operational protocol mandates: (1) Immediate verification of sensor integrity, (2) Scheduling a 15-minute tactical respiratory reset (resonant breathing at 0.1 Hz / 6 breaths/min), and (3) Workload throttling during critical operational tasks.

evidence_references.observed_value:
[Biomedical Knowledge | Autonomic Neurocardiology > Autonomic Nervous System Regulation and Acute Stress Markers]
Title: Autonomic Nervous System Regulation and Acute Stress Markers
Domain: Autonomic Neurocardiology
Citation: AAS-NLSD-2023-V2.1-P44

Acute physiological stress induces simultaneous sympathetic activation and parasympathetic vagal withdrawal. This autonomic state is characterized by an elevated instantaneous heart rate, marked reduction in beat-to-beat variability (RMSSD collapse below 20 ms), and rapid bursts of skin conductance (phasic EDA spikes). Resting RMSSD reflecting cardiac parasympathetic tone must be distinguished from transient task-related reductions.

evidence_references.observed_value:
[Biomedical Knowledge | Human Thermoregulation > Thermoregulatory Dynamics and Core-to-Peripheral Heat Flux]
Title: Thermoregulatory Dynamics and Core-to-Peripheral Heat Flux
Domain: Human Thermoregulation
Citation: JAP-THERM-2022-771

Peripheral skin temperature exhibits gradual thermodynamic drift under steady ambient conditions. Acute rates of change exceeding 0.50 C/min indicate rapid environmental displacement, intense evaporative cooling, or severe cutaneous vasoconstriction due to acute adrenergic surges. Baseline normothermic skin temperature typically ranges from 32.5 C to 35.0 C depending on skin-contact sensor placement.
